newsitem.title: USA: S. Calif. water line construction set for 1997.
newsitem.headline: S. Calif. water line construction set for 1997.

text.p: The construction of a major water line that will help to provide dependable supplies for southern California residents will begin in early 1997, the Metropolitan Water District's board of directors said on Tuesday.

The so-called Inland Feeder, a nearly 43-mile complex of tunnels and pipelines, will connect the state water project aqueduct in San Bernardino County with the Colorado River aqueduct in Riverside County.
John Wodraska, MWD's general manager, said project construction would create thousands of new jobs while pumping hundreds of millions of dollars into the region's economy.

Tuesday's board action on the nearly $1.2 billion project means 2004 is the target date for the Inland Feeder to become operational. Construction is expected to begin as early as January 1997, with the digging of the first tunnel segment under the San Bernardino National Forest, the water district said.

The Metropolitan Water District is a regional water agency which imports water from northern California and the Colorado River, and delivers it on a wholesale basis to the coastal plain of southern California.

Through its 27 member public agencies, the district provides almost 60 percent of the water used by nearly 16 million people living in portions of Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego and Ventura counties.
